prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The manifesto sets out a clear, long‑term plan for a stronger, fairer, more prosperous Britain under “strong and stable” leadership to secure the best Brexit deal and make the most of its opportunities for ordinary, working families. It rejects ideological extremes, embraces government as a force for good, and commits to governing from the mainstream in the interests of the whole United Kingdom, building a Great Meritocracy where success rests on talent and hard work, not privilege.

It identifies five giant challenges—maintaining a strong economy; delivering Brexit in a changing world; overcoming enduring social divisions; responding to an ageing society; and harnessing fast‑changing technology—backed by a modern industrial strategy. The Conservatives promise sound public finances, low taxes, effective regulation, free trade, and growth spread across every region. They will raise the National Living Wage, strengthen rights in the gig economy, tackle tax avoidance, protect pensions, and reform corporate governance (binding votes on executive pay, pay ratios, and stronger worker voice on boards). A major push on R&D, skills, infrastructure and cheaper, reliable energy (including an independent energy cost review, offshore wind leadership and carefully regulated shale) underpins national productivity. Investment will continue in HS2, Northern Powerhouse Rail, Heathrow expansion, roads, electric vehicles, and digital connectivity. Small businesses will benefit from simpler taxes, prompt payment, and a stronger voice in public procurement.

Brexit will be smooth and orderly: a deep and special partnership with the EU, control of laws and immigration, protection of workers’ rights, an open Irish border, and a parliamentary vote on the final deal. The UK will leave the single market and customs union while seeking a comprehensive free trade and customs agreement; “no deal is better than a bad deal.” EU law will be repatriated via a Great Repeal Bill. The Union will be strengthened, with no second Scottish independence referendum now, more devolution within a clear UK framework, and a new UK Shared Prosperity Fund.

Security will be guaranteed with strong defence (meeting NATO 2% and rising), renewal of Trident, modernised forces and support for veterans. Law and order will be reinforced (a national infrastructure police force, tougher action on economic crime, prisons that punish and reform) and leadership against modern slavery sustained.

To build the world’s Great Meritocracy, the manifesto expands good school places (more free schools, lifting the ban on new selective schools with conditions), a knowledge‑rich curriculum, fairer funding, and world‑class technical education (T‑levels, institutes of technology, 3 million apprenticeships). It targets social injustices—closing gender and race gaps, a new Mental Health Bill, stronger disability rights, a landmark Domestic Violence and Abuse Bill, and a drive to end rough sleeping. Immigration will be controlled and reduced to sustainable levels, while integrating divided communities and countering extremism.

The generational contract will be restored through fiscal responsibility, a new pensions Double Lock from 2020, and a sustainable social care settlement (a £100,000 assets floor, the option to defer payments so no one must sell their home in their lifetime, and means‑testing Winter Fuel Payments). The NHS will receive at least £8bn more over five years, more staff, better buildings and technology, faster access to new treatments, seven‑day services, and major improvements in mental health and cancer care.

A Digital Charter will make Britain the best place to start and grow a digital business and the safest place online, with stronger data rights (including deletion at 18), a new data protection law, tough action on online harms, full‑fibre and 5G rollout, and digital government by default.

This is a plan to unite the nation and seize a global future—forward, together.
